title: Recovery from a dense lisse open
statement:
Use the finite-field, smooth-curve and coefficient conventions of [def-wf-middle-extension]. Let $C_0$ be a smooth curve over $k_0$, let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ be a dense open immersion, and let $\mathcal F$ be a lisse $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-sheaf on all of $C_0$ in the convention of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. Then the adjunction unit [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]
$$\eta_{j,\mathcal F}:\mathcal F\longrightarrow j_*j^*\mathcal F$$
is an isomorphism, where $j_*$ is ordinary sheaf direct image, as in [def-wf-middle-extension].

proof.text: By [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves], represent $\mathcal F$ over a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ by a lisse integral system $\mathcal L=(L_n,t_n)$, with $L_n$ a finite locally constant module sheaf over the finite ring $\Lambda_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. We will prove that the actual units $u_n:L_n\to j_*j^*L_n$ are isomorphisms for every $n$, and then construct their compatible inverse system. The finite coefficient level may change its trivializing cover with $n$; no finite cover trivializing $\mathcal F$ is assumed.

source.place: Proof, Step 3 (lisse sheaves extend from a dense open)

proof.text: The field $k_0$ is Noetherian (its ideals are $0$ and $k_0$), and its spectrum is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian. Since $C_0$ is of finite type over $k_0$ in [def-wf-middle-extension], [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $C_0$ Noetherian. By [lem-sc-smooth-normal] it is normal. The normal-Noetherian decomposition in [rem-pc-regular-normal] therefore writes $C_0$ as finitely many open-and-closed normal integral components $C_a$. Density of $U_0$ implies that $U_0\cap C_a$ meets every nonempty open of each $C_a$. The case $C_0=\varnothing$ has only the unique sheaf morphism, which is invertible; henceforth we treat the nonempty components.

source.place: Proof, Step 0 (normality), with the normal-Noetherian decomposition of Stacks Tag 033M

proof.text: Fix $n$ and put $L=L_n$. Apply [fin2-lem-lisse-trivialized-finite-etale] on $C_0$ to choose a finite etale surjection $p:P\to C_0$ such that $p^*L$ is constant with finite module fibre on each connected component. The hypotheses are exactly the finite-type-over-a-field hypothesis of Step 2 and the finite-ring, finite-locally-constant hypotheses of Step 1. The scheme $P$ is Noetherian: finiteness in [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] gives, over each affine $\operatorname{Spec}A$ in $C_0$, an affine inverse image $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ finite as an $A$-module. Its module generators also generate it as an $A$-algebra, since their linear span already contains every element of $B$. Thus $p$ is of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applies with base $C_0$.

source.place: Proof, Step 3 (lisse sheaves extend from a dense open)

proof.text: For each $a$, $P_a=p^{-1}C_a$ is open and closed in the Noetherian scheme $P$, hence Noetherian. Apply [lem-fin-etale-normal-components] to the etale morphism $P_a\to C_a$: its base is normal integral and its source is Noetherian, as required. This decomposes $P$ into finitely many open-and-closed normal integral connected components $Q_b$, on each of which $L|_{Q_b}=\underline{M_b}$ with $M_b$ finite. Put $V_b=Q_b\times_{C_0}U_0$. For any nonempty open $O\subseteq Q_b$, its image in $C_0$ is nonempty and open by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map], so meets the dense open $U_0$; a preimage in $O$ of such a point lies in $V_b$. Thus $V_b$ is a nonempty dense open of $Q_b$. The family $Q_b\to C_0$ is an etale covering, since its images together are the image of the surjection $p$.

source.place: Proof, Step 3 (lisse sheaves extend from a dense open)

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction], etale pullback is restriction of the sheaf to the localized etale site, and the open-adjunction unit is the restriction map on sections. Together with [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], this identifies the restriction of $u_n$ to $(Q_b)_{\mathrm{Et}}$, on every etale object $T\to Q_b$, with
$$L(T)\longrightarrow L(T\times_{C_0}U_0)=L(T\times_{Q_b}V_b).$$
Under the trivialization $L|_{Q_b}=\underline{M_b}$, this is the canonical map $\underline{M_b}_{Q_b}\to(v_b)_*\underline{M_b}_{V_b}$. All hypotheses of [lem-fin-normal-constant-open-image] hold: $Q_b$ is Noetherian, normal and integral, $V_b$ is nonempty open, and $M_b$ is a finite module. That node makes this very map an isomorphism. Its inverse respects the module action because it is inverse to a module-linear isomorphism; no freeness of $M_b$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 09Z5, lemma-push-constant-sheaf-from-open, assertion (2); unit normalization from the existing etale-restriction node

proof.text: We now glue the inverses by the sheaf equalizer of [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], using the covering of [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. For an arbitrary etale $W\to C_0$ and a section $s$ of $j_*j^*L$ on $W$, pull $s$ back to the covering $W_b=W\times_{C_0}Q_b$. Step 5 supplies a unique preimage $r_b\in L(W_b)$. On $W_b\times_WW_c$, the two restrictions of these preimages have the same image, namely the restriction of $s$. This overlap is an etale object over $Q_b$, so Step 5 also gives injectivity there; the preimages therefore agree. The equalizer glues them to a unique $r\in L(W)$. Its image is $s$, since the images agree after the covering and the target is a sheaf. If two sections of $L(W)$ have the same image, Step 5 makes them equal on all $W_b$, hence equal on $W$. We have proved bijectivity on every $W$; the inverses commute with restrictions and module operations by uniqueness. Thus they define an inverse sheaf morphism $u_n^{-1}$.

source.place: Proof, Step 3 (lisse sheaves extend from a dense open)

proof.text:
Write $v_n=u_n^{-1}$. Naturality of section restriction gives $u_n t_n=(j_*j^*t_n)u_{n+1}$, so multiplying by $v_n$ on the left and $v_{n+1}$ on the right gives
$$t_n v_{n+1}=v_n(j_*j^*t_n).$$
The $v_n$ therefore form a morphism of inverse systems, inverse to $(u_n)_n$. Ordinary direct image on systems is obtained by applying its section formula at each level [def-wf-middle-extension, def-weil-pbc-direct-image]; in this case its output system is adic because it is isomorphic, compatibly with transitions, to $\mathcal L$. This is not an assertion that arbitrary direct images of adic systems remain adic. Under the rationalization and finite-extension colimit of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves], the two inverse equations remain inverse equations, giving $\mathcal F\simeq j_*j^*\mathcal F$. The map is the unit, since its finite-level components are the actual units. The construction is natural in $\mathcal F$: if $h:L\to L'$ then $u'h=(j_*j^*h)u$ implies $h v=v'(j_*j^*h)$. Consequently any supplied Weil descent isomorphism also commutes with the unit and its inverse.
